title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
why: A-type coding-agent harness on a physical social robot: agents build a verified atomic-capability library from official documentation, compose skills to solve tasks, then optimize completed programs on user-specified metrics and distill reusable skills for later tasks.
mechanism: A plugin-based framework lets coding agents construct a control program from official documentation and verify candidate capabilities on a physical Misty II robot. Verified capabilities go into an atomic capability library and are combined with existing skills to solve tasks. After completion, the system can collect execution data, measure user-specified metrics, iteratively improve task programs, and distill reusable skills into a skill library for future tasks.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): evaluated on a physical Misty II with Claude Code and Codex, which constructed 109 and 107 verified atomic capabilities respectively. Both complete all 28 AutoMisty benchmark tasks and seven additional tasks beyond AutoMisty's capabilities. Optimization is reported to improve all seven evaluated metrics across five tasks (e.g., dialogue response latency decreases by 52% and 71%). Reusing skills from one optimized dialogue task is reported to reduce latency by 33% to 72% in three other dialogue tasks without further optimization. Numeric tables unread.

title: RESET: One Demonstration, One Verified World, Self-Improved Skills Across Embodiments
why: A-type self-improvement of modular skill code: one real demonstration is used to rebuild a verified world and a frozen success criterion, after which LLM coding agents evolve task graphs and skill programs from per-node failure evidence, then deploy frozen code with zero runtime LLM calls and transfer the verified world to unseen robots without new demonstrations.
mechanism: RESET reconstructs a contact-rich world and derives a frozen read-only success criterion from a single real demonstration (Rebuild); checks that world against the demonstration by open-loop replay and silhouette consistency (Examine); evolves modular white-box task graphs and skill code from per-node failure evidence (Self-improve); deploys the frozen code on real robots with zero runtime LLM calls (Execute); and shares the verified world and criterion with unseen robots without new demonstrations (Transfer). The source robot's kinematics are treated as decoupled from the demonstration.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on 8 manipulation tasks, each rebuilt from one real demonstration, RESET achieves 97% average success on unseen layouts in simulation, versus 27% for zero-shot code, 31% for per-task fine-tuned pi0.5 policies, and 50% for Diffusion Policy. Defect-injection results are described qualitatively. Without target demonstrations, 3 heterogeneous robots acquire the same skills in the shared world (a similar-arm robot copies 95% of skill functions unchanged). In real-robot experiments the programs run on 4 robots and succeed in 80% of 280 trials. Numeric tables unread.

title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
why: A-type in-harness RL for compact VLMs that manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tool calls: supervised fine-tuning on teacher demonstrations is followed by multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, plus a LiteHarness memory layer that keeps interaction context compact.
mechanism: Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, a compact open-weight VLM is further trained with multi-turn reinforcement learning on task-outcome rewards for tool-calling robot manipulation, without relying on a VLA or world-action model. LiteHarness uses hierarchical memory to keep multi-turn interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): with Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis reports that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to 4×, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Numeric tables unread.

title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
why: A-type composition harness around frozen VLA skills under an agentic planner: policy-measured 3D skill envelopes are exposed as classical CHECK/FREE tools so that VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation while code repairs out-of-distribution seam states.
mechanism: The Skill Envelope is a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Each envelope is exposed as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions). The intended division of labor is that frozen VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation while code repairs out-of-distribution seam states; the rigidity of a frozen skill is used to make its trajectory predictable in advance. The tools are used for skill ordering and code repair under an agentic planner.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on LIBERO-Goal with frozen π0.5, the envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793). Using it for skill ordering and code repair is reported to lift success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Numeric tables unread.

title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
why: A-type coding-agent loop that writes programmatic policies for dexterous bimanual manipulation without demonstrations: parallel exploration agents search for skills and compositions, a distilling agent condenses successes into a task library and one program, and the program is then refined under randomized layouts.
mechanism: Coding agents develop a programmatic policy in two stages without demonstrations. During exploration, multiple agents explore in parallel for task skills and ways to compose them, and a distilling agent condenses successful attempts into a task library and one program. During refinement, this program is improved through randomized layouts for robustness and execution efficiency.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): in simulation, PyRUA-Dex achieves a score of 72.9 on Bench2Dex and 81.0% success on DexJoCo under full randomization, reported as ahead of every trained policy on both benchmarks. In real-world experiments on a bimanual platform with two 22-DoF hands, the system is reported to learn piano, calligraphy, and other tasks, with learning a new piece from sheet music taking as little as 30 minutes. title: RegHarness: Regulating What Code-as-Policy Agents Keep from Steps to Skills
why: A-type two-level harness that governs persistence for code-as-policy robot agents: a run-time verifier plus task-long LLM auditor decide which steps are committed within a trial, while a coding agent may propose skill/primitive/rule revisions between runs that stay disabled until explicitly enabled.
mechanism: RegHarness is a two-level harness for the RATs agent team that does not rely on a VLA policy or demonstrations. Within each trial, run-time governance evaluates each proposed step from a reset scene, replaying committed steps, and a fixed-rule controller commits the step only when both RATs' verifier and a task-long LLM auditor approve it. Between runs, a coding agent uses logged failures to develop and test revisions to skills, primitives, and rules, which remain disabled by default until explicitly enabled by the authors.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): using a single low-cost model across all run-time roles, RegHarness achieves an 87.8% success rate (158/180) on paired LIBERO-PRO trials, compared with 39.4% for RATs, and a 72.0% success rate on MolmoSpaces trials. title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
why: A-type agentic manipulation harness that keeps a foundation model frozen while retaining execution knowledge across attempts: a self-evolving programmatic policy acts from current observations, and a persistent action-effect bank records measured effects, including failures, to revise procedures when they meet uncovered conditions.
mechanism: SEEK retains both procedures and measured action effects across attempts while keeping the underlying multimodal foundation model fixed. A Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As those procedures run, a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB) records measured effects, including failed attempts. Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): on RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. Numeric tables unread.

title: A Simple Yet Effective Agent for Open-World Aerial Object Search
why: A-type minimal training-free aerial search agent around a frozen off-the-shelf VLM: current-view target assessment is separated from history-conditioned action selection, with local geometry, depth-based halt checks, and measured execution feedback in a closed loop that does not keep a persistent spatial map.
mechanism: SimpleUAV is built around a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model. It separates current-view target assessment from history-conditioned action selection, combining fresh candidate evidence with lightweight search context. Local geometry converts visual selections into bounded straight-line movements, depth-based checks halt blocked segments, and measured execution feedback guides subsequent decisions. The closed loop is designed to sustain search without persistent spatial maps or task-specific training.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): SimpleUAV achieves 41.61% success rate on UAV-ON and 11.98% on AerialDojo-200K, compared with 23.80% and 3.20% for the strongest prior baselines. With limited benchmark-specific adaptation, the same core agent is reported to transfer to aerial VLN on TravelUAV, improving Full SR by at least 19.66% across all three splits under L1 assistance. title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
why: A-type recursive harness-policy co-evolution: a coding agent searches Code / Code+ICL / Code+Policy routes from policy failures and consolidates verified solutions into skills, routing, and memory (P2H), then verified trajectories supervise the policy with Counterfactual Preference Distillation (H2P), closing a reciprocal loop without additional human demonstrations.
mechanism: In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy then supplies stronger motor skills for subsequent search, and remaining failures redirect harness evolution.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): through recursive co-evolution without additional human demonstrations, RoboEvo^2 improves standalone success from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% on LIBERO-PRO, with similar gains and reduced agentic costs on RoboTwin C2R. Further experiments are reported to demonstrate autonomous task acquisition, cross-embodiment harness transfer, and 95.0% hybrid success on the Unitree G1-D. Numeric tables unread.

title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
why: A-type training-free LLM manipulation agent: a multimodal LLM writes a sparse ordered sequence of 6-DoF keyposes, a motion planner interpolates them, noisy depth-query tools ground the keyposes, and the agent reflects on rollouts to distill per-task rules from execution feedback.
mechanism: A multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. The agent decides the number and spacing of keyposes. Keyposes are grounded with sparse depth queries from noisy sources such as multi-view triangulation, stereo, or monocular depth. The agent also improves from execution feedback, reflecting on its own rollouts and distilling a few rules per task.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): SOLVE reaches 74.5% on RoboDojo and 84.5% on RoboLab, with only $1.7 per episode on average, reported as 12× less than previous dense-control agent policies. On a real robot, the same agent achieves an 88% success rate (75 of 85 episodes) over 16 challenging zero-shot tasks. Numeric tables unread.

title: Toward Agentic Robotics: A Large-Scale Study of Harness Design for Robot-Use Agents
why: A/B-type large-scale controlled study of policy-harness design for robot-use agents that combine VLM reasoning and tools with VLA/WAM control; the reference recipe X-Harness composes the findings without weight updates.
mechanism: The paper treats agentic robots as a combination of VLM reasoning and perception with precise VLA/WAM control through a policy harness. Seven controlled studies over a large rollout budget are used to specify what structure the VLM's policy code needs, where VLA manipulation needs help from tools and policy code, and when to involve the VLM at test time. The reference recipe X-Harness is reported to compose these findings without weight updates.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): evaluation covers over 470,000 rollouts across eight simulation benchmarks, six VLMs, and 15 VLA/WAM checkpoints. X-Harness is reported to lift base policies by up to +42.8 points across memory, reasoning, and domain shifts. Numeric tables unread.

title: Cairn: Object-Centric 3D Trajectory Priors for Steering Frozen VLAs
why: A-type test-time steering of a frozen VLA: a small 3D trajectory prior samples SE(3) object trajectories around obstacles, and bidirectional feedback between the prior and the frozen VLA guides denoising without weight updates.
mechanism: Cairn keeps the VLA frozen and steers it at test time along learned 3D trajectories of the object in its gripper. A small prior reads point clouds of the scene and the held object, along with its pose when grasped and the instruction, and samples SE(3) trajectories up to release that lead around obstacles and through gaps. The prior and the VLA form two levels of a hierarchical planner with bidirectional feedback: the VLA's intended motion chooses and reshapes the trajectories, and the chosen trajectory pulls the VLA's predicted actions (mapped to the held object's poses through the grasp) toward the next waypoint, while the VLA's weights stay untouched.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): across 1,941 held-out LIBERO scenes with displaced objects and obstacles, Cairn raises the success rate of a frozen π0.5 from 24.5% to 95.1%, above that of a π0.5 fine-tuned on the training layouts, without hurting standard LIBERO. On LIBERO-PRO it raises success from 27.3% to 38.0%, and from 54.4% to 81.1% on the episodes it steers. On a real Franka, with a prior trained purely in simulation, it is reported to guide the frozen DROID π0.5 around an obstacle and to a far placement where it otherwise fails. Numeric tables unread.

title: Robo-Harness K1: Harnessing Robot-Use Agents via Perception Augmentation
why: Update of the known Robo-Harness K1 perception-as-tools robot-use-agent framework already in the corpus: the v2 abstract restates the tool set, revises the reported LIBERO-PRO numbers, and newly reports RoboCasa mobile-manipulation transfer, real-world Piper-arm trials, and mixed-environment post-training results.
mechanism: Corpus/latest known version is 2609.29389v1 (submitted Thu, 24 Sep 2026). The Wednesday 25 Nov 2026 catchup replacement listing announced v2 (submitted Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:26:00 UTC). The paper remains a robot-use-agent harness that exposes perception as tools (region grounding, calibrated depth and geometry, persistent visual anchors, and projected grasp candidates) for a VLM that measures the scene, chooses a motion, and measures again. The v2 abstract tightens this loop description and adds real-robot and multi-environment post-training claims that were not in the v1 abstract.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (v2 abstract): on LIBERO-PRO, K1 raises Gemini 3.7 Flash from 16.7% to 71.7% and GPT-6 Astra from 63.3% to 93.3%, with the largest gains on spatial tasks (the v1 abstract instead reported Gemini with K1 at 77.8% and Astra improved to 88.9%, and compared Gemini+K1 with Astra under an RGB-only harness at 61.1%). Without fine-tuning, the Gemini agent is now also reported to transfer to mobile manipulation in RoboCasa, in addition to three RoboSuite arms and dual-arm RoboTwin. New real-world experiments on a Piper arm complete eight of nine concluded trials across three tasks. Agentic post-training of Qwen3.5-9B on 107 successful episodes still reports 44.2% on new initial states and 13.9% on held-out task conditions versus 30.2% and 0.0% for OpenVLA; v2 additionally reports that mixed training on traces from four environments raises held-out accuracy from 11.1% to 27.8% and RoboSuite success from 28.3% to 50.0%.
